schema_note: Standalone JSON study schema; no claim of compatibility with an unspecified external MRS schema.
scope: Lemma 2.2 and explicitly derived radial-contact consequences only.

definitions.rho_c: The unique positive scalar rho with norm(c+rho*v)=1 for unit v.
definitions.ray_convention: t>=0; t>0 is equivalent under norm(c)<1

assumptions.text: X is a real normed space. Assume X nonzero when a nonempty sphere is required.
X is a real Hilbert space; needed only for D8 and Example 2's formula.
All directions v,w mentioned are in S_X and all ray parameters are real.
c,d in X with norm(c),norm(d)<=q<1 for one common q.
Directions u,z are nonzero; normalization is not assumed.

background.name: Norm axioms
background.statement: Positive definiteness, absolute homogeneity, triangle inequality.

background.name: Norm convexity
background.proof: Apply the triangle inequality and nonnegative homogeneity.

background.name: Real intermediate value theorem
background.statement: A continuous real function with values on opposite sides of a level attains that level on the interval.

background.name: Compactness of a bounded closed real interval
background.statement: Every sequence in a closed bounded real interval has a convergent subsequence in the interval.

background.name: Sequential criterion for metric continuity
background.statement: For maps between metric spaces, sequential continuity at every point is equivalent to continuity.

background.name: Real mean value theorem
background.statement: A derivative bounded in absolute value by L implies L-Lipschitz continuity on an interval.

background.name: Cauchy Schwarz inequality
background.statement: In a real Hilbert space, abs(inner(x,y)) <= norm(x)*norm(y).

theorems.title: Existence of radial contact
theorems.statement: For every unit v there exists R>0 with norm(c+R*v)=1.
theorems.proof: h(t)=norm(c+t*v) is 1-Lipschitz. h(0)=r<1 and h(U)>=U-r=1. Apply the real intermediate value theorem on [0,U]; the root is positive.

theorems.title: Uniqueness of radial contact
theorems.statement: There is exactly one R>0 with norm(c+R*v)=1.
theorems.proof: If 0<s<t are contacts, c+s*v=(1-s/t)c+(s/t)(c+t*v), hence 1<=r+(s/t)(1-r)<1, a contradiction.

theorems.title: Uniform radius bounds
theorems.statement: a <= rho_c(v) <= U, where r=norm(c)<1, a=1-r, U=1+r.
theorems.proof: At a contact R, 1<=r+R gives R>=a, and 1>=R-r gives R<=U.

theorems.title: Continuous dependence on the direction
theorems.statement: rho_c:S_X->(0,infinity) is continuous in the norm topology.
theorems.proof: For v_n->v, radii lie in [a,U]. Any convergent subsequence of radii has limit L and norm(c+L*v)=1, hence L=rho_c(v). A sequence failing convergence has a subsequence staying away from rho_c(v), whose convergent further subsequence contradicts that conclusion.

theorems.title: Radial crossing estimate
theorems.statement: For R=rho_c(v) and all t>=0, abs(norm(c+t*v)-1)>=(a/R)*abs(t-R). Norm is strictly below 1 for t<R and strictly above 1 for t>R.
theorems.proof: For t<=R, convexity gives h(t)<=r+a*t/R. For t>=R, apply convexity at c+R*v=(1-R/t)c+(R/t)(c+t*v), then rearrange to h(t)>=r+a*t/R.

theorems.title: Lipschitz radius and reciprocal radius
theorems.statement: For R=rho_c(v), S=rho_c(w): abs(R-S)<=R*S/a*norm(v-w); abs(1/R-1/S)<=norm(v-w)/a; abs(R-S)<=U^2/a*norm(v-w).
theorems.proof: The norm residual at c+S*v is at most S*norm(v-w). D1 bounds the same residual below by (a/R)*abs(S-R). Divide and use R,S<=U.

sharpness.radius: Optimal uniform constant U^2/a over normed spaces and centers of prescribed norm r, for each 0<r<1.
sharpness.reciprocal: Optimal uniform constant 1/a in the same class, for each 0<r<1.
sharpness.zero_center: rho_0 is constant; the optimal radius and reciprocal-radius constants are 0.

theorems.title: Lipschitz contact map
theorems.proof: For R>=S, R*v-S*w=S*(v-w)+(R-S)*v. Bound by S*norm(v-w)+abs(R-S); swap roles otherwise, use D2 and U+U^2/a=2U/a.
theorems.optimality: Not claimed optimal. E3 gives a universal lower bound U^2/a for r>0; the proved upper bound is 2U/a.

theorems.title: Bi Lipschitz sphere parametrization
theorems.statement: P_c:S_X->S_X is bijective with inverse Q_c(x)=(x-c)/norm(x-c). Q_c is 2/a-Lipschitz; (a/2)*norm(v-w)<=norm(P_c(v)-P_c(w)).
theorems.proof: norm(x-c)>=a. Uniqueness gives P_c(Q_c(x))=x, and Q_c(P_c(v))=v directly. For nonzero b,d, normalization has distance <=2*norm(b-d)/max(norm(b),norm(d)) by adding and subtracting d/norm(b) when norm(b)>=norm(d). Apply to x-c,y-c.

theorems.title: Uniform center and direction perturbation estimates
theorems.statement: For norm(c),norm(d)<=q<1, a_q=1-q, U_q=1+q, eta=norm(c-d), delta=norm(v-w): abs(rho_c(v)-rho_d(w))<=U_q/a_q*eta+U_q^2/a_q*delta; norm(P_c(v)-P_d(w))<=2/a_q*eta+2*U_q/a_q*delta.
theorems.proof: At S=rho_d(w), abs(norm(c+S*v)-1)<=eta+S*delta. Apply D1 at center c, then R,S<=U_q and 1-norm(c)>=a_q. Contact difference is at most eta+U_q*delta+abs(R-S).

theorems.title: Nonzero unnormalized directions
theorems.statement: For u!=0, tau_c(u)=rho_c(u/norm(u))/norm(u) and a/norm(u)<=tau_c(u)<=U/norm(u). For u,z!=0, abs(tau_c(u)-tau_c(z))<=U^2/(a*norm(u)*norm(z))*norm(u-z). The contact distance is <=2U/(a*max(norm(u),norm(z)))*norm(u-z).
theorems.proof: Normalize the ray for existence, uniqueness and bounds. D1's convexity proof works with arbitrary nonzero u. Comparing the residual at tau_c(z) yields abs(tau_c(u)-tau_c(z))<=tau_c(u)*tau_c(z)/a*norm(u-z). If norm(u)>=norm(z), decompose contact difference as tau_c(u)*(u-z)+(tau_c(u)-tau_c(z))*z and substitute the bounds.
theorems.scaling: For lambda>0, tau_c(lambda*u)=tau_c(u)/lambda and the contact point is unchanged. Negative lambda reverses the ray. u=0 has no contact.
theorems.annulus_constants: On norm(u)>=m>0, tau_c is U^2/(a*m^2)-Lipschitz and the contact map is 2U/(a*m)-Lipschitz.

theorems.title: Bisection and residual certification
theorems.statement: For unit v, [a,U] brackets rho_c(v). After n exact bracket halvings, midpoint error <=r/2^n. For any t>=0, abs(t-rho_c(v))<=U/a*abs(norm(c+t*v)-1).
theorems.proof: At a the norm is <=r+a=1; at U it is >=U-r=1. D1 determines the side of the unique root by the sign. Each valid bisection halves width from initial 2r. Rearrange D1 and use R<=U for the residual bound.
theorems.approximate_norm_caution: If hhat has certified absolute error eps, the root error is <=U/a*(abs(hhat-1)+eps). An error interval containing 1 does not justify choosing a bisection side.
theorems.execution: Specification only; no numerical experiment or proof checker was run.

theorems.title: Hilbert specialization
theorems.statement: In a real Hilbert space, rho_c(v)=-b+sqrt(b^2+1-r^2), b=inner(c,v). It is r*(1+r)-Lipschitz on the unit sphere.
theorems.proof: Solve t^2+2*b*t+r^2-1=0; r<1 makes exactly one root positive. For |b|<=r, F'(b)=-1+b/sqrt(b^2+1-r^2) has absolute value <=1+r. Combine the real mean value theorem with abs(inner(c,v-w))<=r*norm(v-w).
theorems.optimality: The Hilbert-specific constant is valid; optimality is not claimed.
